introduction.p: We will explore the area formula in this preview activity.

statement.p: Find the area of the following parallelograms.

description.p: A parallelogram with vertices at the origin, (1,0), (1,1), and (0,1).

image.shortdescription: A rectangle having sides of length two and three

description.p: A parallelogram with vertices at the origin, (2,0), (2,3), and (0,3).

image.shortdescription: A square whose sides make 45 degree angles with the coordinate axes.

description.p: A parallelogram with vertices at the origin, (1,-1), (2,0), and (1,1).
A parallelogram with vertices at the origin, (2,0), (3,2), and (1,2).
A parallelogram with vertices at the origin, (2,0), (4,2), and (0,2).

solution.p:
We find the following areas.
A 1\times1 square has area 1.
A 2\times3 rectangle has area 6.
The square has side length \sqrt{2} giving an area of 2.
If we consider the horizontal length as the base, we see that b=h=2 so that the area is 4.
In the same way, we can consider both the base and height to be 2 so that the area is 4.

sidebyside.p: Explain why the area of the parallelogram formed by the vectors \vvec and \wvec_1 is the same as that formed by \vvec and \wvec_2.

image.shortdescription: A horizontal vector with two vectors ending on the same horizontal line.

description.p: A horizontal vector \vvec and two vectors \wvec_1 and \wvec_2 that end on the same horizontal line.

solution.p: If we consider the base to be the length of \vvec, then the height, which is the perpendicular distance to its parallel side, is the same in both parallelograms.
